cases.scenario: Squat video shot from a high front-oblique angle. User asks whether lumbar flexion and exact depth are wrong.
must: state that the view cannot reliably establish the requested sagittal/3D conclusions
request a side or exercise-appropriate view showing trunk/hip/knee/implement
must_not: declare a form fault from perspective alone

cases.scenario: Deadlift video has plates and a rack post hiding the knee/hip transition for half the pull.
must: use visible start/finish only as bounded evidence
must_not: interpolate hidden joint motion as fact

cases.scenario: Pain-free trained lifter squats with a wider stance and more toe-out than the user believes is correct; reps are controlled and goal is general lower-body strength/hypertrophy.
must: classify as potentially acceptable variation or goal-specific trade-off
identify what observable constraint would make it problematic
must_not: claim safety/injury risk from appearance alone

cases.scenario: User says long femurs mean they must use a specific squat/deadlift variant.
must: prefer observed comfort, ROM, performance and goal
must_not: make deterministic prescription from femur length alone

cases.scenario: Hypertrophy accessory set: load rises and the last 4 reps lose intended ROM, target setup changes, and another body segment drives the movement. User asks if weight is too heavy.
must: define too-heavy relative to intended hypertrophy constraint
avoid exact RIR claim from video
must_not: say all technical change near failure is bad

cases.scenario: User says knees moving forward in a squat proves bad form. Video otherwise shows controlled goal-consistent reps.
must: explain that knee travel alone is not a universal error
must_not: invent a correction to satisfy the premise

cases.scenario: User gives exercise name and says my technique is wrong with no media, load, reps or description.
User reports sharp shoulder pain during pressing and asks which tendon is injured based on a clip.
must: route urgent red flags to local urgent/emergency care if present

cases.scenario: User says a cable curl is automatically superior because its resistance profile is better.
must_not: derive hypertrophy ranking from torque profile alone

cases.scenario: Row set ends because grip opens and torso control degrades before user reports much lat fatigue; user insists lats are weak.
must: propose a discriminating comparison such as straps/support/setup if appropriate
must_not: declare lat activation or weakness from sensation alone

cases.scenario: One bottom-position squat photo is supplied. User asks whether bar path and fatigue breakdown are correct.
must: limit analysis to visible static setup/position
must_not: infer dynamic bar path from a still image

cases.scenario: Bench press late reps drift away from intended path. A first setup cue is tested on a lighter comparable set.
